summary: All departures from U.S. airports are held. Flights already in the air are continuing to land. The FAA has not announced a lift time.
cause: FAA and the White House describe a telecommunications outage affecting all en-route air traffic control centers. DHS says there is no indication of a cyberattack.

timeline.text: About 1,000 flights are airborne toward U.S. airports. A normal Friday evening has more than 4,500.
Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin says there is no indication of a cyberattack or terror threat, calling it "just a telecommunications outage."
International departures begin leaving case by case. Etihad's Boston to Abu Dhabi flight gets airborne.
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy says the stop follows "a communication issue impacting all Air Route Traffic Control Centers." FAA technicians are investigating.
FAA Command Center orders every U.S. airport ground stopped "due to extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety." 4,042 flights are airborne toward U.S. airports at that moment.
